chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said:

I said to him: A waterskin containing water—if a dead mouse, rat, or sparrow falls into it? He said: If it decomposes in it, then do not drink from its water and do not perform wudu (ablution) from it. But if it is not decomposed, then drink from it and perform wudu (ablution), and cast away the carcass when you remove it fresh. The same applies to the jar, the large water vessel, the waterskin, and similar containers of water. He said: And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: If the water is more than a rāwiyah, nothing that decomposes in it or does not decompose renders it impure, unless an odor comes to it that overpowers the smell of the water.

So this report may be understood such that his statement, “a rāwiyah of water,” refers to when its amount is a kurr; for when it is like that, nothing that falls into it renders it impure. And his statement, “if it decomposes in it, then do not drink and do not perform wudu (ablution),” is understood as referring to when one of the qualities of the water changes. The same applies to the jar, the large water vessel, and the waterskin. No one may say that the jar, the large water vessel, the waterskin, and the rāwiyah cannot contain a kurr of water, because the report does not say that a single jar has that ruling; rather, it mentioned them with the definite article, and that indicates generality according to many of the people of language. If that possibility exists, then it does not conflict with the reports we have presented earlier.

key_terms.أَوْصَافِ الْمَاءِ: the properties or characteristics of the water, such as smell, color, or taste
key_terms.تَفَسَّخَ: decomposed or disintegrated in the water
key_terms.حُبُّ الْمَاءِ: a large vessel or container for water
key_terms.رَاوِيَةٌ: a waterskin or water-container used as a measure here
key_terms.كُرًّا: the legal measure of abundant water that is not easily rendered impure

ai.seo_question: Does a dead animal falling into water make the water impure in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the fiqh of water becoming impure when a dead animal falls into it, especially in relation to decomposition and changes in the water’s properties. It also presents a reconciliatory explanation that water reaching the measure of kurr is not rendered impure by such contact unless one of its qualities changes, making it significant for rulings on ritual purity and wudu (ablution).
